name: Load Transfer Portability and Contrast
goal: Same free-body load-transfer question, but classified along TWO independent dimensions rather than one ranking. First, patch-portability to a warpmpm-like MPM implementation that has particle-grid transfer but NO pressure field: momentum-exchange and penalty mechanisms are highest-priority candidates, cut-cell or SDF geometric reconstruction is partially portable, and pressure-integration mathematics is not directly implementable. Second, citation and contrast value for explaining limitations, where pressure/stress-integration, immersed-boundary and fictitious-domain methods stay prominent even when not portable because they give rigorous contrast with a missing pressure solve, constraint force or reaction accumulator.
summary: For a warpmpm-like implementation with particle-grid transfers but NO pressure solve, the most directly PORTABLE load-transfer routes are conservative momentum/impulse exchange and penalty reactions, NOT pressure integration [Gao18b, Che24g, Nak21]. PORTABLE: [Gao18b] exchanges momentum through two MPM background grids; [Che24g] generalizes to impulse-to-velocity transfer and path-integrated coupling forces; [Hu18] supplies particle-grid compatibility and an SDF-style interface construction; [Nak21] supplies particle-to-surface penalty contact suitable for accumulating reaction impulses on a free rigid body. SPH boundary-particle pairwise forces give a body resultant and lever-arm torque that can be accumulated directly [Aki12, Ami15, Li23e, Neg24]; strong implicit pressure/contact variants [Gis19b, Pro23b] are robust but need a pressure or global constraint solve. Exact linear and angular momentum preservation in particle-grid transfer is documented by [Jia16]; LBM momentum exchange gives an explicit force-and-torque analogue [Gio14]. CONTRAST (not portable, but they expose what a pressureless MPM lacks): [Kal14b] solves fluid pressure plus immersed-boundary Lagrange multipliers to enforce no-slip exactly; [Glo01] uses fictitious-domain multipliers as the hydrodynamic reaction; [Nan17] computes net force and torque from moving-control-volume balance; [Ji23] shows a pressure-free control-volume momentum balance, conceptually transferable but not natively particle-grid. [Fan20] and [Hu18] mark the portability boundary: interface quadrature and compatibility are reusable, pressure-only coupling is not. TOP-RANKED: Nan17, Li23e, Bec09, Aki12, Rob08b, Kal14b.
